01-01.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous
01-01.quote: "We keep what we have only with vigilance..."

01-02.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
01-02.quote: Sometimes when we pray, a remarkable thing happens; we find the means, the ways and the energies to perform tasks far beyond our capacities.

01-03.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
01-03.quote: "We eventually redefine our beliefs and understanding to the point where we see that our greatest need is for knowledge of God's will for us and the strength to carry that out."

01-04.quote: "Today secure in the love of the fellowship, we can finally look another human being in the eye and be grateful for who we are."

01-05.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
01-05.quote: "We can enjoy our families in a new way and may become a credit to them instead of an embarrassment or a burden."

01-07.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
01-07.quote: Narcotics Anonymous offers addicts a program of recovery which is more than just a life without drugs. Not only is this way of life better than the hell we lived, it is better than any life we had ever known.

01-08.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
01-08.quote: "Our spiritual condition is the basis for a successful recovery that offers unlimited growth."

01-09.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
01-09.quote: "Our earliest involvements with others often begin with our sponsor."

01-11.quote: As we develop faith in our daily lives, we find that our Higher Power supplies us with the strength and guidance we need.

01-12.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
01-12.quote: "Having had a spiritual awakening as a result of these steps..."

01-13.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step One
01-13.quote: "Help for addicts begins only when we are able to admit complete defeat."

01-14.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Two
01-14.quote: "Our understanding of a Higher Power is up to us.... The only suggested guidelines are that this Power be loving, caring, and greater than ourselves."

01-15.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Two
01-15.quote: We grow to feel comfortable with our Higher Power as a source of strength. As we learn to trust this Power, we begin to overcome our fears of life.

01-16.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Five
01-16.quote: We feared that if we ever revealed ourselves as we were, we would surely be rejected. ... Our fellow members do understand us.

01-17.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eight
01-17.quote: As we realize our need to be forgiven, we tend to be more forgiving. At least, we know we are no longer intentionally making life miserable for people in our recovery.

01-18.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Ten
01-18.quote: "Continuing to take a personal inventory means that we form a habit of looking at ourselves, our actions, our attitudes, and our relationships on a regular basis."

01-19.quote: "When we stop living in the here and now, our problems become magnified unreasonably."

01-20.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
01-20.quote: "Narcotics Anonymous offers only one promise, and that is freedom from active addiction..."

01-21.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition One
01-21.quote: "Unity is a must in Narcotics Anonymous."

01-22.location: Chapter Three: Why Are We Here?
01-22.quote: This is a program for doing just those things.

01-23.quote: "Lack of daily maintenance can show up in many ways."

01-24.location: Chapter One: Who Is An Addict?
01-24.quote: "Our disease isolated us... Hostile, resentful, self-centered, and self-seeking, we cut ourselves off from the outside world."

01-25.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
01-25.quote: We see it happening among us every day. This miraculous turnabout is evidence of spiritual awakening.

01-26.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step One
01-26.quote: "The spiritual part of our disease is our total self-centeredness."

01-27.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
01-27.quote: "We learn new ways to live. We are no longer limited to our old ideas."

01-28.quote: We never fully recover, no matter how long we've been clean.

01-29.quote: "Do we understand that we have no real control over drugs?"

01-30.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
01-30.quote: "We must give freely and gratefully that which has been freely and gratefully given to us."

01-31.quote: "Just for today I will have faith in someone in NA who believes in me and wants to help me in my recovery."

02-01.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step One
02-01.quote: We felt different. Upon working this step, we affirmed our surrender to the principles of Narcotics Anonymous, and only then did we begin to overcome the alienation of addiction.

02-02.quote: Goodwill is best exemplified in service and proper service is "Doing the right thing for the right reason".

02-03.location: Chapter Two: What Is The Narcotics Anonymous Program?
02-03.quote: "Anyone may join us, regardless of age, race, sexual identity, creed, religion, or lack of religion."

02-04.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Ten
02-04.quote: "For us, recovery is more than just pleasure."

02-05.quote: "We are grateful that we were made so welcome at meetings that we felt comfortable."

02-06.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition One
02-06.quote: "We had convinced ourselves that we could make it alone and proceeded to live life on that basis. The results were disastrous and, in the end, each of us had to admit that self-sufficiency was a lie."

02-07.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
02-07.quote: "... we have found a loving, personal God to whom we can turn."

02-10.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
02-10.quote: "In recovery, our ideas of fun change."

02-11.location: Chapter One: Who Is An Addict?
02-11.quote: We have become very grateful in the course of our recovery. ... We have a disease from which we do recover.

02-12.location: Chapter One: Who Is An Addict?
02-12.quote: We regretted the past, dreaded the future, and we weren't too thrilled about the present.

02-13.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous
02-13.quote: "As long as the ties that bind us together are stronger than those that would tear us apart, all will be well."

02-14.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Three
02-14.quote: "The right to a God of your understanding is total and without any catches. Because we have this right, it is necessary to be honest about our belief if we are to grow spiritually."

02-15.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
02-15.quote: "The last thing we expected was an awakening of the spirit."

02-17.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Three
02-17.quote: They can be analyzed, counseled, reasoned with, prayed over, threatened, beaten, locked up, or whatever, but they will not stop until they want to stop.

02-19.quote: Relapse is never an accident. Relapse is a sign that we have had a reservation in our program.

02-20.location: Chapter Three: Why Are We Here?
02-20.quote: Through our inability to accept personal responsibilities we were actually creating our own problem.

02-21.quote: "Self-pity is one of the most destructive of defects; it will drain us of all positive energy."

02-22.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Ten
02-22.quote: We continued to take personal inventory, and when we were wrong promptly admitted it.

02-23.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Twelve
02-23.quote: "Anonymity is the spiritual foundation of all our traditions, ever reminding us to place principles before personalities."

02-24.location: Chapter Three: Why Are We Here?
02-24.quote: "Personality change was what we really needed. Change from self-destructive patterns of life became necessary"

02-25.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Five
02-25.quote: It would be tragic to have it all written down and then shove it in a drawer. These defects grow in the dark, and die in the light of exposure.

02-26.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eight
02-26.quote: The Eighth Step is a big change from a life dominated by guilt and remorse.

02-27.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Ten
02-27.quote: We examine our actions, our reactions, and our motives. We often find that we've been "doing" better than we've been "feeling".

02-28.quote: "Our newly found faith serves as a firm foundation for courage in the future."

02-29.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
02-29.quote: Our disease has been arrested and now anything is possible. We become increasingly open-minded which opens the door for new ideas, in all areas of our lives.

03-01.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Three
03-01.quote: We realize that what brought us to this Program is still with us today and will continue to guide us if we allow it.

03-02.location: Chapter Three: Why Are We Here?
03-02.quote: "Any form of success was frightening and unfamiliar"

03-03.quote: "There will be times, however, when we really feel like using. We want to run, and we feel lousy. We need to be reminded of where we came from and that it will be worse this time. This is when we need the program the most"

03-05.quote: When a need arises for us to admit our powerlessness, we may first look for ways to exert power against it. Exhausting these ways, we begin sharing with others and find hope.

03-07.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Ten
03-07.quote: The good times can also be a trap; the danger is that we may forget that our first priority is staying clean.

03-08.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
03-08.quote: "What we want most is to feel good about ourselves."

03-09.quote: "In the past, we made simple situations into problems; we made mountains out of molehills."

03-10.quote: The steps are our solution. They are our survival kit. They are our defense, for addiction is a deadly disease. Our steps are the principles that make our recovery possible.

03-11.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eight
03-11.quote: "It will not make us better people to judge the faults of another. It will make us feel better to clean up our lives..."

03-12.quote: "Many times in our recovery the old bugaboos will haunt us. Life may again become meaningless, monotonous, and boring."

03-14.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
03-14.quote: Also, our inventories usually include a lot of material on relationships.

03-15.quote: The get-togethers after our meetings are good opportunities to share things we didn't get to discuss during the meeting.

03-16.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
03-16.quote: The purpose of a searching and fearless moral inventory is to sort through the confusion and the contradiction of our lives so that we can find out who we really are.

03-17.quote: "Those who make it through these times show a courage not their own."

03-18.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
03-18.quote: There is a special feeling that comes over a person with our disease when they discover that there are other people who share their difficulties, past and present.

03-19.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
03-19.quote: "A simple, honest message of recovery from addiction rings true."

03-20.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Two
03-20.quote: Most of us have no trouble admitting that addiction had become a destructive force in our lives. Our best efforts resulted in ever greater destruction and despair. At some point we realized we needed the help of some Power greater than our addiction.

03-21.location: Chapter One: Who Is An Addict?
03-21.quote: Addiction is a disease which involves more than simple drug use.

03-22.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Seven
03-22.quote: In our addiction, we were dependent on people, places and things. We looked to them to support us and supply the things we found lacking in ourselves.

03-23.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
03-23.quote: We can put in the footwork and accept what's being freely given to us on a daily basis.

03-24.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step One
03-24.quote: "It is not where we were that counts, but where we are going."

03-25.quote: From the isolation of our addiction, we find a fellowship of people with the common bond of recovery. ... Our faith, strength and hope come from people sharing their recovery and from our relationship with the God of our own understanding.

03-27.location: Chapter Two: What Is The Narcotics Anonymous Program?
03-27.quote: "In accordance with the principles of recovery, we try not to judge, stereotype, or moralize with each other."

03-28.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
03-28.quote: We may fear that being in touch with our feelings will trigger an overwhelming chain reaction of pain and panic.

03-29.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
03-29.quote: We are able to set aside some of our personal preference, if necessary, to do this because we learn that God's will consists of the very things we care most about. God's will for us becomes our own true will for ourselves.

03-30.quote: "Gradually as we become more God-centered than self-centered, our despair turns to hope."

03-31.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
03-31.quote: "Our real value is in being ourselves."

04-01.location: Chapter One: Who Is An Addict?
04-01.quote: Some of us first saw the effects of addiction on the people with whom we were close. We were very dependent on them to carry us emotionally through life. We felt angry, disappointed and hurt when they had other interests, friends and loved ones.

04-02.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Eleven
04-02.quote: Our public image consists of what we have to offer which is a successful proven way of maintaining a drug-free lifestyle.

04-03.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
04-03.quote: The idea of a spiritual awakening takes many different forms in the different personalities we find in the fellowship.

04-04.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
04-04.quote: Remember that we-not our doctor-are ultimately responsible for the risk we expose ourselves to.

04-06.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
04-06.quote: "On a practical level, changes occur because what's appropriate to one phase of recovery may not be for another."

04-07.location: Chapter Two: What Is The Narcotics Anonymous Program?
04-07.quote: This mass of intensive first-hand experience in all phases of illness and recovery is of unparalleled therapeutic value. We are here to share freely with any addicts who want it.

04-08.quote: "We come to know happiness, joy, and freedom."

04-10.quote: "We must use what we learn or we will lose it, no matter how long we have been clean."

04-11.quote: "A new idea cannot be grafted onto a closed mind.... Open-mindedness leads us to the very insights that have eluded us during our lives."

04-12.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
04-12.quote: However, all spiritual awakenings have some things in common. Among them are an end to loneliness and a sense of direction in our lives.

04-13.location: Chapter Three: Why Are We Here?
04-13.quote: This approval-seeking carried us further into our addiction.

04-14.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Six
04-14.quote: "Do we really want to be rid of our resentments, our anger, our fear?"

04-15.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Three
04-15.quote: We have come to enjoy clean living and want more of the good things that the N.A. fellowship holds for us.

04-16.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
04-16.quote: Today we seek solutions, not problems. We try what we learn on an experimental basis.

04-18.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Seven
04-18.quote: "We humbly asked Him to remove our shortcomings."

04-19.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Six
04-19.quote: So many times we addicts have sought the rewards of hard work without the labor.

04-21.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step One
04-21.quote: "We have found that we had no choice except to completely change our old ways of thinking or go back to using."

04-22.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Seven
04-22.quote: "This is our road to spiritual growth."

04-23.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Three
04-23.quote: Many of us understand God to be simply whatever keeps us clean.

04-24.location: Chapter One: Who Is An Addict?
04-24.quote: Our lives have become useful, through abstinence and by working the Twelve Steps of Narcotics Anonymous.

04-25.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
04-25.quote: "Recovery is a reality for us today."

04-27.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
04-27.quote: "We want to look our past in the face, see it for what it really was, and release it so we can live today."

04-28.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
04-28.quote: We can also use the steps to improve our attitudes. Our best thinking is what got us into trouble. We recognize the need for change.

04-29.quote: Living just for today relieves the burden of the past and the fear of the future. We learned to take whatever actions are necessary and leave the results in the hands of our Higher Power.

04-30.quote: "Ongoing recovery is dependent on our relationship with a loving God who cares for us and will do for us what we find impossible to do for ourselves."

05-02.quote: "There is one thing more than anything else that will defeat us in our recovery; this is an attitude of indifference or intolerance toward spiritual principles."

05-03.location: Gratitude Prayer - After Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
05-03.quote: "My gratitude speaks when I care and when I share with others the NA way."

05-04.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Five
05-04.quote: "Each group has but one primary purpose-to carry the message to the addict who still suffers."

05-06.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
05-06.quote: In time, we relax and enjoy the atmosphere of recovery.

05-08.quote: We have learned that it is O.K. to not know all the answers, for then we are teachable and can learn to live our new life successfully.

05-09.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
05-09.quote: "We sit down with a notebook, ask for guidance, pick up our pen, and start writing."

05-10.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Six
05-10.quote: We examine the Fourth Step inventory and get a good look at what these defects are doing to our lives. We begin to long for freedom from these defects.

05-11.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Ten
05-11.quote: A lot of our chief concerns and major difficulties come from our inexperience with living without drugs. Often when we ask an "oldtimer" what to do we are amazed at the simplicity of the answer.

05-12.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
05-12.quote: "For meditation to be of value, the results must show in our daily lives."

05-13.quote: "The progression of recovery is a continuous uphill journey."

05-14.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Two
05-14.quote: "Insanity is repeating the same mistakes and expecting different results."

05-15.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
05-15.quote: As we approach this step, most of us are afraid that there is a monster inside us that, if released, will destroy us.

05-16.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
05-16.quote: "God's will for us becomes our own true will for ourselves."

05-17.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Six
05-17.quote: "We were entirely ready to have God remove all these defects of character."

05-18.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Nine
05-18.quote: "We made direct amends to such people wherever possible, except when to do so would injure them or others."

05-19.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
05-19.quote: We review our past performance and our present behavior to see what we want to keep and what we want to be rid of.

05-20.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
05-20.quote: We find ourselves doing things that we never thought we would be doing, and enjoying them.

05-21.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
05-21.quote: "Meetings keep us in touch with where we've been, but more importantly with where we could go in our recovery."

05-22.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
05-22.quote: The steps lead to an awakening of a spiritual nature. This awakening within is evidenced by change in our lives.

05-23.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Nine
05-23.quote: "We want to be free of our guilt, but we don't wish to do so at the expense of anyone else."

05-24.quote: "As we grow, we learn to overcome the tendency to run and hide from ourselves and our feelings."

05-26.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Two
05-26.quote: "Our understanding of a Higher Power is up to us.... We can call it the group, the program, or we can call it God."

05-27.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Three
05-27.quote: ". . . the decision to ask for God's help is our greatest source of strength and courage."

05-28.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Seven
05-28.quote: We examined our lives and discovered who we really are. To be truly humble is to accept and honestly try to be who we are.

05-29.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
05-29.quote: "We believe that our Higher Power will take care of us."

05-30.quote: "Sharing with others keeps us from feeling isolated and alone."

05-31.quote: "We live a day at a time but also from moment to moment. When we stop living in the here and now, our problems become magnified unreasonably"

06-01.location: Chapter Two: What Is The Narcotics Anonymous Program?
06-01.quote: We don't have to be clean when we get here, but after the first meeting, we suggest that newcomers keep coming back and come back clean. We don't have to wait for an overdose, or jail sentence, to get help from Narcotics Anonymous, nor is addiction a hopeless condition from which there is no recovery.

06-02.location: Chapter One: Who Is An Addict?
06-02.quote: We wanted an easy way out and some of us thought of suicide. ... When we did seek help, we were really only looking for the absence of pain.

06-03.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Nine
06-03.quote: We can only make our amends to the best of our ability.

06-04.location: Chapter Three: Why Are We Here?
06-04.quote: "Our negative sense of self has been replaced by a positive concern for others."

06-05.quote: "Although honesty is difficult to practice, it is most rewarding."

06-06.quote: "The Twelve Steps of Narcotics Anonymous are a progressive recovery process established in our daily living."

06-07.quote: "Just for today I will have faith in someone in NA who believes in me and wants to help me in my recovery"

06-09.quote: "Lost dreams awaken and new possibilities arise."

06-10.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
06-10.quote: When we finally get our own selfish motives out of the way, we begin to find a peace we never imagined.

06-11.quote: "As we recover, we gain a new outlook on being clean.... Life can become a new adventure for us."

06-12.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
06-12.quote: "Yes, we are a vision of hope..."

06-13.location: Chapter Two: What Is The Narcotics Anonymous Program?
06-13.quote: "The program works a miracle in our lives.... We become free to live."

06-14.quote: If we maintain our spiritual condition daily, we find the pain and confusion easier to deal with.

06-15.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Six
06-15.quote: Many of us cling to our fears, doubts, and self-loathing or hatred of others because there is a certain distorted security in familiar pain. It seems safer to hold on to what we know than to let go of it for the unknown.

06-16.quote: Some things we must accept, and others we can change. The wisdom to know the difference comes with growth in our spiritual program.

06-17.quote: "Reaching out is the beginning of the struggle that will set us free. It will break down the walls that imprison us."

06-18.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Nine
06-18.quote: "Indirect amends may be necessary where direct ones would be unsafe or endanger other people."

06-19.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
06-19.quote: "We find that when we lose self-obsession, we are able to understand what it means to be happy, joyous, and free."

06-20.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
06-20.quote: For some, prayer is asking for God's help, and meditation is listening for God's answer. ... Quieting the mind through meditation brings an inner peace which brings us into contact with the God within.

06-21.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
06-21.quote: "We have been experts at self-deception and rationalization."

06-22.quote: In our recovery, we find it essential to accept reality. Once we can do this, we do not find it necessary to use drugs in an attempt to change our perceptions.

06-23.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step One
06-23.quote: "We didn't stumble into this fellowship brimming with love, honesty, open- mindedness, or willingness.... When we were beaten, we became willing."

06-24.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Twelve
06-24.quote: "ever reminding us to place principles before personalities."

06-25.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Two
06-25.quote: The process of coming to believe is a restoration to sanity. The strength to move into action comes from this belief.

06-26.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Three
06-26.quote: "Our fears are lessened and faith begins to grow as we learn the true meaning of surrender: We are no longer fighting fear, anger: guilt, self-pity, or depression."

06-27.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Seven
06-27.quote: When someone points out a shortcoming, our first reaction may be one of defensiveness. ... There will always be room for growth.

06-28.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
06-28.quote: "Working with others is only the beginning of service work."

06-29.quote: "Complacency is the enemy of members with substantial clean time. If we remain complacent for long, the recovery process ceases."

06-30.quote: "Our newly found faith serves as a firm foundation for courage in the future"

07-02.quote: "Our personal stories may vary in individual pattern, but in the end we all have the same thing in common."

07-03.quote: "Many of us have found that setting aside quiet time for ourselves is helpful in making conscious contact with our Higher Power:"

07-04.quote: "We learn that conflicts are a part of reality, and we learn new ways to resolve them instead of running from them."

07-05.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
07-05.quote: The nature of our belief will determine the manner of our prayers and meditations.

07-06.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eight
07-06.quote: The main thing this step does for us is to help build an awareness that, little by little, we are gaining new attitudes about ourselves and how we deal with other people.

07-07.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
07-07.quote: "One aspect of our spiritual awakening comes through the new understanding of our Higher Power that we develop by sharing another addict's recovery."

07-09.quote: "...the time has come when that tired old lie, "Once an addict, always an addict," will no longer be tolerated by either society or the addict himself. We do recover."

07-11.quote: "We share comfort and encouragement with others."

07-12.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Three
07-12.quote: "We were trapped by our need for the instant gratification that drugs gave us."

07-13.quote: "If we are hurting, and most of us do from time to time, we learn to ask for help."

07-14.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step One

07-15.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eight
07-15.quote: "We made a list of all persons we had harmed and became willing to make amends to them all."

07-17.quote: Do we fully accept the fact that our every attempt to stop using or control our using failed?

07-18.location: Chapter Three: Why Are We Here?
07-18.quote: "Our disease always resurfaced or continued to progress until, in desperation, we sought help from each other in Narcotics Anonymous."

07-19.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Seven
07-19.quote: Those dreams we gave up long ago can now become realities.

07-20.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step One
07-20.quote: "We admitted that we were powerless over our addiction, that our lives had become unmanageable."

07-21.quote: If, after a period of time, we find ourselves in trouble with our recovery, we have probably stopped doing one or more of the things which helped us in the earlier stages of our recovery.

07-22.quote: "For us, to use is to die, often in more ways than one."

07-23.quote: Our own self-will leads to many problems in our recovery; we want and demand that things go our way. We should know from our past experience that our way of doing things did not work.

07-24.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Five
07-24.quote: "...we covered low self-esteem by hiding behind phony images that we hoped would fool people. The masks have to go."

07-25.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
07-25.quote: "Having had a spiritual awakening as a result of these steps, we tried to carry this message to addicts, and to practice these principles in all our affairs."

07-26.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step One
07-26.quote: "Help for addicts begins only when we are able to admit complete defeat. This can be frightening, but it is the foundation on which we have built our lives."

07-27.location: Chapter Two: What Is The Narcotics Anonymous Program?
07-27.quote: "After coming to NA, we found ourselves among a very special group of people who have suffered like us and found recovery. In their experiences, freely shared, we found hope for ourselves. If the program worked for them, it would work for us."

07-28.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Five
07-28.quote: "We feared that if we ever revealed ourselves as we were, we would surely be rejected."

07-29.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eight
07-29.quote: "As we realize our need to be forgiven, we tend to be more forgiving."

07-30.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Ten
07-30.quote: Continuing to take a personal inventory means that we form a habit of looking at ourselves, our actions, our attitudes and our relationships on a regular basis.

07-31.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
07-31.quote: "Narcotics Anonymous offers only one promise and that is freedom from active addiction, the solution that eluded us for so long."

08-01.location: Chapter One: Who Is An Addict?
08-01.quote: Our addiction had enslaved us. We were prisoners of our own mind, condemned by our own guilt.

08-02.quote: "When we feel trapped or pressured, it takes great spiritual and emotional strength to be honest."

08-03.quote: "Many of us would have had nowhere else to go if we could not have trusted NA groups and members."

08-04.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Five
08-04.quote: "Addicts tend to live secret lives.... It is a great relief to get rid of all our secrets and to share the burden of our past."

08-05.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
08-05.quote: Shaping our thoughts with the spiritual ideals that we are moving toward, we are freed to become who we want to be.

08-06.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
08-06.quote: "Since the beginning of our recovery, we have found that joy doesn't come from material things but from within ourselves."

08-07.quote: "We focus on anything that isn't going our way and ignore all the beauty in our lives."

08-08.quote: ".. we accept responsibility for our problems and see that we're equally responsible for our solutions."

08-09.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
08-09.quote: We begin to see that God's love has been here all the time, just waiting for us to accept it.

08-10.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
08-10.quote: "Most of us pray when we are hurting. We learn that if we pray regularly, we won't be hurting as often or as intensely."

08-11.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
08-11.quote: "Through active listening, we hear things that work for us."

08-13.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
08-13.quote: By giving unconditional love in the fellowship, we become more loving, and in the sharing of spiritual growth we become more spiritual.

08-14.location: Chapter Two: What Is The Narcotics Anonymous Program?
08-14.quote: We don't have to settle for the limitations of the past. We can examine and re-examine all our old ideas and constantly improve on them or replace them with new ones.

08-15.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
08-15.quote: "We found that we do not recover physically, mentally, or spiritually overnight."

08-16.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Seven
08-16.quote: This is our road to spiritual growth. We change every day to gradually, carefully and simply pull ourselves out of the isolation and loneliness of addiction into the mainstream of life. ... This comes not from wishing, but from action and prayer.

08-17.quote: "A symptom of our disease is alienation, and honest sharing will free us to recover"

08-18.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
08-18.quote: "The way to remain a productive, responsible member of society is to put our recovery first."

08-19.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
08-19.quote: We apply our efforts to our most obvious problems and let go of the rest. We do the job at hand and as we progress, new opportunities for improvement present themselves.

08-20.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
08-20.quote: Often we have to face some type of crisis during our recovery, such as death of a loved one, financial difficulties or divorce.

08-22.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
08-22.quote: "We recognize our spiritual growth when we are able to reach out and help others."

08-23.quote: "Before we got clean, most of our actions were guided by impulse. Today, we are not locked into this type of thinking."

08-24.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
08-24.quote: "We learn to be careful of praying for specific things."

08-25.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Nine
08-25.quote: "We are achieving freedom from the wreckage of our past."

08-26.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Ten
08-26.quote: "We continued to take personal inventory and when we were wrong promptly admitted it."

08-27.location: Chapter Three: Why Are We Here?
08-27.quote: "Change from self-destructive patterns of life became necessary"

08-28.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Five
08-28.quote: "These defects grow in the dark and die in the light of exposure."

08-29.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eight
08-29.quote: The Eighth Step is a big change from a life dominated by guilt and remorse. Our futures are changed because we don't have to avoid those we have harmed, and as a result of this step, we've received a new freedom which contributes to the end of isolation.

08-30.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Ten
08-30.quote: We examine our actions, our reactions, and our motives. We often find that we've been "doing" better than we've been "feeling".

08-31.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
08-31.quote: Hopeless living problems became joyously changed. Our disease has been arrested and now anything is possible.

09-01.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
09-01.quote: "We become able to make wise and loving decisions based on principles and ideals that have real value in our lives."

09-02.quote: Daily practice of our Twelve Step program enables us to change from what we were to what our Higher Power would have us become.

09-03.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Twelve
09-03.quote: Humility is a by-product which allows us to grow and develop in an atmosphere of freedom and removes the fear of becoming known by our employers, families, or friends as addicts.

09-04.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Nine
09-04.quote: "We try to remember that when we make amends we are doing it for ourselves."

09-05.location: Chapter Three: Why Are We Here?
09-05.quote: We found that we suffered from a disease, not a moral dilemma. We were critically ill, not hopelessly bad.

09-06.location: Chapter Two: What Is The Narcotics Anonymous Program?
09-06.quote: "We have learned from our group experience that those who keep coming to our meetings regularly stay clean."

09-07.location: Chapter Two: What Is The Narcotics Anonymous Program?
09-07.quote: Living this Program gives us a relationship with a Power greater than ourselves, corrects defects, leads us to help others, and where there has been wrong, teaches us the spirit of forgiveness.

09-08.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Six
09-08.quote: "We need not lose faith when we become rebellious"

09-09.quote: One of the biggest stumbling blocks seems to be in placing unrealistic expectations on ourselves or others.

09-10.quote: "We learn that a simple, loving hug can make all the difference in the world"

09-11.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
09-11.quote: "We learn to become flexible.. As new things are revealed, we feel renewed."

09-13.location: Chapter Three: Why Are We Here?
09-13.quote: "We had to have something different, and we thought we had found it in drugs."

09-14.quote: "Eventually we are shown that we must get honest, or we will use again."

09-15.quote: Sometimes we forget and we think that if we can just get enough food or enough sex or enough money we'll be satisfied and everything will be all right.

09-16.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
09-16.quote: "Emotional balance is one of the first results of meditation, and our experience bears this out."

09-17.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Five
09-17.quote: We may think that we have done enough by writing everything down, and this is a mistake we cannot afford.

09-18.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
09-18.quote: "One of the most profound changes in our lives is in the realm of personal relationships."

09-21.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
09-21.quote: Prayer takes practice and it may be well to remind ourselves that skilled people were not born with their skills.

09-22.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
09-22.quote: "Life takes on a new meaning when we open ourselves to this gift."

09-23.location: Chapter Two: What Is The Narcotics Anonymous Program?
09-23.quote: "In accordance with the principles of recovery, we try not to judge, stereotype, or moralize with each other."

09-24.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Two
09-24.quote: "The only suggested guidelines are that this Power be loving, caring, and greater than ourselves. We don't have to be religious to accept this idea. The point is that we open our minds to believe."

09-25.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
09-25.quote: "We may fear that being in touch with our feelings will trigger an overwhelming chain reaction of pain and panic."

09-26.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eight
09-26.quote: "It will not make us better people to judge the faults of another."

09-27.quote: "There is something in our self-destructive personalities that cries for failure."

09-28.quote: "Gradually as we become more God-centered than self centered, our despair turns to hope."

09-29.quote: "When we stop living in the here and now, our problems become magnified unreasonably."

09-30.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
09-30.quote: "Our real value is in being ourselves."

10-01.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
10-01.quote: "We learn that pain can be a motivating factor in recovery."

10-02.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
10-02.quote: We grasp the limitless strength provided for us through our daily prayer and surrender so long as we keep faith and renew it.

10-03.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
10-03.quote: "Our egos, once so large and dominant, now take a back seat because we are in harmony with a loving God. We find that we lead richer, happier, and much fuller lives when we lose self-will."

10-04.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
10-04.quote: When we first begin to enjoy relief from our addiction, we run the risk of assuming control of our lives again. We forget the agony and pain we have known.

10-05.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eight
10-05.quote: A problem many of us have with the Eighth Step and the admission of the harm is the belief that we were victims, not victimizers, in our addiction. ... We cut away all our justifications and all our ideas of being a victim.

10-06.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eight
10-06.quote: Projecting about actually making amends can be a major obstacle both in making the list and in becoming willing.

10-07.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Seven
10-07.quote: "As recovering addicts, we find that we are still dependent, but our dependence has shifted from the things around us to a loving God and the inner strength we get in our relationship with Him."

10-08.quote: "We suspect that if we do not use what we have, we will lose what we have."

10-09.quote: "We emphasize setting our house in order because it brings us relief."

10-10.quote: "Before we got clean, most of our actions were guided by impulse. Today, we are not locked into this type of thinking."

10-11.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
10-11.quote: Our best thinking is what got us into trouble. ... Recovery is an active change of our ideas and attitudes.

10-12.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
10-12.quote: When we admit that our lives had become unmanageable, we don't have to argue our point of view. ... We no longer have to be right all the time.

10-13.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
10-13.quote: "Words cannot describe the sense of spiritual awareness that we receive when we have given something, no matter how small, to another person."

10-15.location: Chapter One: Who Is An Addict?
10-15.quote: "We did not choose to become addicts."

10-16.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
10-16.quote: "praying only for knowledge of His will for us and the power to carry that out."

10-17.quote: "Everything we know is subject to revision, especially what we know about the truth."

10-18.quote: "Although 'politics makes strange bedfellows,' as the old saying goes, addiction makes us one of a kind."

10-19.quote: "... we could feel time, touch reality, and recognize spiritual values long lost to many of us."

10-20.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
10-20.quote: Enforced morality lacks the power that comes to us when we choose to live a spiritually-oriented life.

10-22.quote: "Our disease is so cunning that it can get us into impossible situations."

10-23.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
10-23.quote: By the surrender of our control, we gain a far greater power.

10-24.quote: We are not responsible for our disease, only our recovery. As we begin to apply what we have learned, our lives begin to change for the better.

10-25.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Twelve
10-25.quote: "Anonymity is the spiritual foundation of all our traditions, ever reminding us to place principles before personalities."

10-27.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
10-27.quote: "We want to look our past in the face, see it for what it really was, and release it so we can live today."

10-28.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
10-28.quote: "We can also use the steps to improve our attitudes."

10-29.quote: "Living just for today relieves the burden of the past and the fear of the future."

10-30.quote: "Our newly found faith serves as a firm foundation for courage in the future."

10-31.quote: "Ongoing recovery is dependent on our relationship with a loving God who cares for us and will do for us what we find impossible to do for ourselves."

11-01.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
11-01.quote: "God helps us as we help each other."

11-02.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
11-02.quote: It makes all the difference to have friends who care if we hurt.

11-03.quote: "We eventually have to stand on our own feet and face life on its own terms, so why not from the start."

11-04.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
11-04.quote: We offer hope for we know that a better way of life is now real for us, and we give love because it was so freely given. New frontiers are open to us as we learn how to love. Love can be the flow of life energy from one person to another.

11-05.quote: "Our Higher power is accessible to us at all times. We receive guidance when we ask for knowledge of God's will for us."

11-06.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Seven
11-06.quote: Humility has a lot to do with getting honest with ourselves, which is something we have practiced from Step One.

11-08.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Two
11-08.quote: "Do I believe it would be insane to walk up to someone and say, "May I please have a heart attack or a fatal accident"

11-09.quote: It is our action that is important. We leave the results to our Higher Power.

11-10.location: Chapter Three: Why Are We Here?
11-10.quote: No matter how far we ran, we always carried the fear with us.

11-11.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Three
11-11.quote: "We surrender quietly and let the God of our understanding take care of us."

11-12.quote: "When we honestly tell our own story, someone else may identify with us."

11-13.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
11-13.quote: "We are not going to be perfect. If we were perfect, we would not be human."

11-14.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Twelve
11-14.quote: When using, our lives became an exercise in survival. Now we are doing much more living than surviving.

11-15.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Three
11-15.quote: "Take my will and my life. Guide me in my recovery. Show me how to live."

11-16.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Seven
11-16.quote: We change every day to gradually, carefully and simply pull ourselves out of the isolation and loneliness of addiction into the mainstream of life.

11-17.quote: "We never have to use again, no matter how we feel. All feelings will eventually pass."

11-18.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Ten
11-18.quote: The Tenth Step can do this for us; it can help us correct our living problems and prevent their recurrence.

11-19.quote: ".... the addict would find from the start as much identification as each needed to convince himself that he could stay clean, by the example of others who had recovered for many years".

11-20.quote: "We weren't oriented toward fulfillment; we focused on the emptiness and worthlessness of it all"

11-21.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Seven
11-21.quote: If they really contributed to our health and happiness, we would not have come to such a state of desperation.

11-22.quote: "As we begin to function in society, our creative freedom helps us sort our priorities and do the basic things first."

11-23.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Three
11-23.quote: The relief of "letting go and letting God" helps us develop a life worth living.

11-24.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
11-24.quote: "We entertained the thought that staying clean was not paying off and the old thinking stirred up self-pity, resentment, and anger."

11-25.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
11-25.quote: Quieting the mind through meditation brings an inner peace which brings us into contact with the God within.

11-27.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Three
11-27.quote: "At times during our recovery, the decision to ask for God's help is our greatest source of strength and courage."

11-28.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Seven
11-28.quote: To be truly humble is to accept and honestly try to be who we are.

11-29.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
11-29.quote: "We believe that our Higher Power will take care of us."

11-30.quote: "Sharing with others keeps us from feeling isolated and alone."

12-01.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
12-01.quote: We begin to pray only for God's will for us. This way we are getting only what we are capable of handling.

12-02.quote: "We have to keep our recovery first and our priorities in order"

12-03.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Six
12-03.quote: "Perhaps for the first time, we see a vision of our new life."

12-04.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
12-04.quote: We now know that if we pray to do God's will, we will receive what is really best for us, regardless of what we think.

12-05.location: Chapter Two: What Is The Narcotics Anonymous Program?
12-05.quote: We have seen the Program work for any addict who honestly and sincerely wants to stop.

12-06.quote: "Relationships can be a terribly painful area."

12-07.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
12-07.quote: We use the tools available to us, and we develop the ability to survive our emotions.

12-08.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Six
12-08.quote: "When we see how our defects exist in our lives and accept them, we can let go of them and get on with our new life."

12-09.location: Chapter Ten: More Will Be Revealed
12-09.quote: This ability is a gift and grows as we grow spiritually. Life takes on a new meaning when we open ourselves to this gift.

12-11.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Four
12-11.quote: "No one is forcing us to give up our misery."

12-12.location: Chapter Three: Why Are We Here?
12-12.quote: "By working the steps, we come to accept a Higher Power's will.... We lose our fear of the unknown. We are set free."

12-13.location: Chapter Two: What Is The Narcotics Anonymous Program?
12-13.quote: "There is only one requirement for membership, the desire to stop using."

12-14.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step One
12-14.quote: Addiction is a physical, mental and spiritual disease, affecting every area of our lives.

12-15.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Eleven
12-15.quote: There is a spiritual principle of giving away what we have been given in Narcotics Anonymous in order to keep it. By helping others to stay clean, we enjoy the benefit of the spiritual wealth we have found.

12-16.quote: "Complacency is the enemy of members with substantial clean time. If we remain complacent for long, the recovery process ceases."

12-17.quote: "Everything that occurs in the course of NA service must be motivated by the desire to more successfully carry the message of recovery to the addict who still suffers."

12-18.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Five
12-18.quote: "The fact that we, each and every group, focus on carrying the message provides consistency; addicts can count on us."

12-19.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
12-19.quote: "Words mean nothing until we put them into action."

12-20.quote: "In living the steps, we begin to let go of our self-obsession."

12-21.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
12-21.quote: Freedom to change seems to come mainly after our acceptance of ourselves.

12-22.quote: "When at the end of the road we find that we can no longer function as a human being, either with or without drugs, we all face the same dilemma.... Either go on as best we can to the bitter ends-jails, institutions, or death-or find a new way to live."

12-23.quote: "We reevaluate our old ideas so we can become acquainted with the new ideas that lead to a new way of life."

12-24.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Five
12-24.quote: "The Twelfth Step of our personal program also says that we carry the message to the addict who still suffers.... The group is the most powerful vehicle we have for carrying the message."

12-25.location: Chapter Six: The Twelve Traditions Of Narcotics Anonymous - Tradition Twelve
12-25.quote: The drive for personal gain in the areas of sex, property and social position, which brought so much pain in the past, falls by the wayside if the principle of anonymity is adhered to.

12-26.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Two
12-26.quote: As we learn to trust this Power, we begin to overcome our fears of life.

12-27.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Two
12-27.quote: The process of coming to believe is a restoration to sanity. The strength to move into action comes from this belief.

12-28.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Three
12-28.quote: "We are no longer fighting fear anger guilt, self-pity, or depression."

12-29.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Seven
12-29.quote: When someone points out a shortcoming, our first reaction may be one of defensiveness. ... If we truly want to be free, we will take a good look at what is pointed out to us.

12-30.location: Chapter Four: How It Works - Step Seven
12-30.quote: This comes not from wishing, but from action and prayer.

12-31.location: Chapter Five: What Can I Do?
12-31.quote: "Working with others is only the beginning of service work."
